view: Core PCE inflation momentum does not roll over on the consensus schedule. The three-month annualised rate stays at or above 3.0% through the November 2026 reference month.
consensus: Philadelphia Fed Survey of Professional Forecasters, Q2 2026 (released 15 May 2026): median core PCE 3.3% Q4/Q4 for 2026 falling to 2.4% Q4/Q4 for 2027. FOMC Summary of Economic Projections, 17 June 2026: median core PCE 3.3% for 2026, 2.5% for 2027, 2.1% for 2028. Both paths require the momentum rate to be decisively through 3% well before the end of 2026.
deviation: Consensus has the run rate through 3% inside two quarters. This desk does not, because the real policy rate is roughly 0.5% (3-month bill 3.87% less core PCE 3.41% at 30 June; 3.96% less 3.41% at the report date) and a stance that is not restrictive does not produce disinflation on a schedule. The consensus path requires the 2026 impulse to be supply-driven and self-reversing without help from policy.
falsifier: Core PCE three-month annualised, computed from PCEPILFE as (level_t / level_t-3)^4 - 1, prints below 3.0% in the BEA Personal Income and Outlays release covering November 2026 data.
position_detail: commodities +5.00pp, held at the 8% line limit
strongest_argument_against: Core PCE at 3.41% year on year is running roughly 80bp ABOVE core CPI at 2.6% for June 2026. That inversion is unusual, since core PCE normally prints below core CPI on weighting and the treatment of shelter. If the wedge is an artifact concentrated in imputed categories such as medical care and financial services, it closes by core PCE falling toward core CPI rather than by core CPI rising, and consensus is right for a reason this desk has not priced.

view: Ten-year inflation compensation is too low. The 10-year breakeven rises to 2.45% or above within twelve months.
consensus: The market itself: T10YIE at 2.24% on 30 June 2026 and 2.20% on 28 July 2026. Against that, the SPF Q2 2026 median 10-year (2026-2035) annual average CPI forecast is 2.40% and PCE 2.22%, and the New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations for June 2026 (released 7 July 2026) puts median three-year expectations at 3.3%, the highest since June 2022, and five-year at 3.0%.
deviation: The market prices CPI at 2.20% for a decade, 20bp below the SPF's own long-run median and 80bp below what households say they expect over five years, at a moment when realised core PCE is 3.41%. This desk is on the forecasters' and households' side of that gap and against the price. The position is expressed by not owning the nominal bond, since the opportunity set contains no TIPS line.
falsifier: T10YIE fails to close at or above 2.45% on any day between 28 July 2026 and 30 June 2027.
strongest_argument_against: A breakeven is not a forecast. It is a forecast less an inflation risk premium plus a TIPS liquidity discount, and the two can be large enough to explain the whole gap without anyone expecting 2.20% inflation. If the liquidity discount on TIPS has widened, the breakeven understates expectations mechanically and there is no view here at all.

view: The FOMC delivers at least one further tightening. The target range is above 3.50-3.75% following the March 2027 meeting.
consensus: New York Fed Survey of Market Expectations, June 2026 (distributed 3 June, 61 of 62 dealers responding): the modal fed funds midpoint is 3.63% at every meeting from June 2026 through March 2027, that is, no change, with easing only from 2027 Q2. Dealers put 9% probability on a hike at the July 2026 meeting. Consensus is genuinely split here: the FOMC's own median dot for end-2026 is 3.8%, above the current 3.625% midpoint, so the committee's own projection is on this desk's side and the sell side is not.
deviation: Against the dealer modal path. The 3-month bill at 3.96% on 27 July sits 33bp above the 3.625% target midpoint, which is not a level a bill market carries into a meeting it expects to be uneventful. This desk reads the bill and the dots rather than the survey. Note honestly that the curve already prices most of this, so the position earns little for being right and the size reflects that.
falsifier: The fed funds target range is still 3.50-3.75% or lower immediately following the March 2027 FOMC meeting.
position_detail: cash +7.00pp, funded from duration, credit and equity
strongest_argument_against: Payroll growth has already halved: the three-month average falls from 188k on the 30 June vintage to 111k once the June print (+57k, released 2 July) enters, and the SPF expects only 34.6k a month across 2026. A committee watching that does not hike, whatever its dots said in June.

view: High yield is not being paid for the risk it carries. The index option-adjusted spread trades above 4.00% at some point within twelve months.
consensus: The market: BAMLH0A0HYM2 at 2.80% on 29 June 2026 and 2.81% on 27 July 2026, the 17th and 21st percentile of the history available to this study. Against that, the SPF Q2 2026 assigns a mean probability of a negative real GDP quarter of 17.9% for 2026 Q2, 25.1% for Q3, 24.5% for Q4 and 25.7% for 2027 Q1.
consensus_verification: [VERIFIED: url above for the SPF probabilities; spread levels are from FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 through taa.pitdata]
deviation: On a standard decomposition, OAS equals the expected default rate times one less recovery, plus whatever premium the buyer demands for illiquidity and volatility. At 40% recovery a 2.81% spread implies a 4.68% annual default rate only if the buyer demands no premium at all. Against a long-run US high yield default rate near 3.5% [RECALLED, Moody's long-run average, not verified in this session] the expected loss is roughly 210bp and the spread leaves about 70bp for everything else. Consensus prices a one-in-four chance of a negative quarter and 70bp of compensation at the same time. Those two cannot both be right.
falsifier: BAMLH0A0HYM2 fails to close at or above 4.00% on any day between 28 July 2026 and 30 June 2027.
strongest_argument_against: Spreads have been rich for most of three years and staying rich is what rich spreads usually do. A percentile computed against a three-year history that is itself entirely a tight-spread regime is close to uninformative about the level, and this desk is using exactly that.

view: No deviation on growth. The underweight rests on what is being paid for the earnings, not on a forecast of them.
consensus: SPF Q2 2026 median real GDP growth 2.2% for 2026 and 1.9% for 2027; FOMC SEP median 2.2% for 2026 and 2.3% for 2027; Atlanta Fed GDPNow at 1.6% for 2026 Q2 as of 27 July 2026.
deviation: This desk accepts the consensus growth number and deviates on price. The dividend-based equity risk premium proxy is 0.91% at 30 June 2026 and 0.67% at the report date, the lowest of the twenty meeting dates in the window and down from 4.26% at the first. The whole of that decline is the real yield rising from (0.85)% to 2.20% while the trailing dividend yield fell from 1.41% to 1.11%. A 2pp trim is the size a valuation observation justifies without a growth view behind it.
falsifier: The proxy, computed as SPY trailing twelve-month dividend yield plus 2.0% assumed real growth less DFII10, rises above 1.50% before 30 June 2027, through a lower price, a higher payout or a lower real yield.
strongest_argument_against: A trailing dividend yield is the wrong numerator for an index that returns most of its cash through buybacks. Total shareholder yield on the S&P 500 is materially higher than 1.11%, so the level of this proxy is too low by construction and only its direction carries information. If the payout mix has shifted further toward buybacks over the window, even the direction is contaminated.
